entries.title: WSJ: Nvidia in Talks to Backstop $250B in OpenAI Data Center Financing — Deepening AI Power Concentration
entries.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia is in talks to guarantee roughly $250B so OpenAI can lease a 10-gigawatt SoftBank-built data center in Ohio (total project cost estimated at $500B+), with separate discussions on up to $350B in chip-purchase financing — a deal that would lock Nvidia and OpenAI into deep financial interdependence and give OpenAI its first owned infrastructure.

links.title: Reuters via Yahoo Finance: Nvidia in talks with OpenAI to guarantee $250B financing

entries.title: Kimi K3 2.8T Open Weights Released on Hugging Face — Largest Open-Weight Model Ever, Safeguards Previously Flagged Failed
entries.summary: Moonshot AI released Kimi K3's full 2.8-trillion-parameter weights at 00:00 UTC July 27, making the largest open-weight model in history freely downloadable under a Modified MIT license despite AISI/CAISI having found its safeguards failed to block offensive cyber attempts in pre-release evaluation.

entries.title: Reddit v. Perplexity: Judge Questions Reddit's Standing to Sue on Users' Behalf at 3-Hour Oral Argument on Motion to Dismiss
entries.summary: Judge Engelmayer (SDNY) held nearly three hours of oral argument on Perplexity's motion to dismiss Reddit's data-scraping suit on July 23, expressing skepticism about whether Reddit has legal authority to assert copyright claims on behalf of its users — a threshold question that will determine the legal viability of RAG-based AI products that rely on scraped public-web data.

entries.title: Debian Opens Formal GR Discussion Period on Whether to Ban All LLM Contributions to the Project
entries.summary: The Debian Project formally opened a General Resolution discussion period on July 24 with four competing proposals — including a complete ban on any LLM-assisted contributions to source packages, documentation, translations, and official communications — raising governance and supply-chain questions for the world's most widely deployed community Linux distribution.

entries.title: Stanford SIEPR Policy Brief: No Aggregate AI Job Displacement Yet, But Early-Career White-Collar Demand Is Eroding
entries.summary: A new SIEPR policy brief synthesizes current empirical evidence and finds no significant aggregate job displacement as of mid-2026, but documents measurably reduced hiring demand for early-career white-collar workers and firms using AI investment as explicit justification for workforce reductions — providing the first rigorous institutional baseline on this question.

links.title: SIEPR: What Is Really Happening to Jobs? Separating AI Hype from Reality

entries.title: Trend Micro: Enterprises Are Missing Four Critical Agentic AI Controls — Inventory, Least-Agency, Supply Chain, and Communication Monitoring
entries.summary: New Trend Micro research identifies four specific control gaps enabling agentic AI systems to act across enterprise environments without meaningful governance visibility, recommending agent inventorying, least-privilege and least-agency policies, supply-chain risk treatment for third-party tools and extensions, and monitoring of inter-agent communication flows as pre-deployment requirements.
